title: AINU opens uro-nephrology hospital in Bhubaneswar, marks entry into Odisha
summary: The new facility takes AHH's investment in AINU to ₹750 crore, with the group aiming to close the financial year with a network of 10 hospitals

contentHtml:
The new facility takes AHH's investment in AINU to ₹750 crore, with the group aiming to close the financial year with a network of 10 hospitals

Asia Healthcare Holdings (AHH) has launched a uro-nephrology hospital under the Asian Institute of Nephrology and Urology (AINU) in Bhubaneswar, marking its entry into Odisha. The launch builds on AHH’s cumulative investment of ₹650 crore in AINU, with a further ₹100 crore committed towards the new facility and other initiatives in the state. AHH aims to close the current financial year with a network of 10 hospitals as part of AINU’s expansion.

AHH’s previous investments have supported AINU’s expansion and the development of its clinical and technological capabilities across the country. These include the addition of 300 beds, expansion of its Banjara Hills facility and the introduction of three robotic surgery programmes.

The Bhubaneswar hospital is AINU’s eighth facility in India, following its presence in Hyderabad, Visakhapatnam, Siliguri and Chennai. It extends the institute’s kidney and urology services to patients across Odisha and neighbouring regions.

The expansion comes against the backdrop of the kidney disease burden in India. According to the ICMR–INDIAB study, published in the Indian Journal of Medical Research, impaired kidney function was identified in 3.2 per cent of the nationally representative study population of 25,408 adults. Odisha was among the states reporting a prevalence of 6 per cent or higher.

The new hospital brings together services across nephrology, urology, uro-oncology, kidney transplantation, dialysis, paediatric urology, andrology and reconstructive urology.

Its infrastructure includes a 12-station haemodialysis unit, three operation theatres, a 100W Holmium laser, a 45W Thulium Fibre Laser, 3D laparoscopy, RIRS, PCNL, an in-house 32-slice CT scanner and video urodynamics. A urological robotic surgery platform is also scheduled to be launched soon. The facility will have nephrology and urology OPDs and an in-house pharmacy.

Speaking about the expansion, Vishal Bali, Executive Director, Asia Healthcare Holdings (AHH), said, “The opportunity in specialised healthcare lies in building institutions that combine deep clinical expertise with the right infrastructure, technology and talent. At AHH, our approach is to strengthen specialised healthcare platforms such as AINU by investing in clinical capabilities, technology and infrastructure to expand access to advanced care across underserved markets. Post the acquisition, we have added 300 beds, enhanced robotic technology and strengthened clinical talent” He also added,* “AINU’s expansion into Odisha is an important step in addressing this gap, while strengthening its presence in Eastern India. We see significant potential in developing specialised centres of excellence that can deliver consistent clinical outcomes and bring advanced healthcare closer to communities. As part of our growth plans, we are on track to close this financial year with a network of 10 hospitals, further strengthening our presence and reach across the country.”*

Sandeep Guduru, Chief Executive Officer, Asian Institute of Nephrology & Urology (AINU), said, “AINU’s entry into Bhubaneswar is a strategic milestone in our growth journey and reinforces our vision of building a wider network of specialised kidney and urology care centres. This is our 8th hospital across the country. As healthcare needs evolve, we believe dedicated centres of excellence can play a vital role in improving access, strengthening patient confidence and delivering consistent standards of care. Our expansion into Odisha is driven by the opportunity to combine clinical expertise, advanced infrastructure and operational excellence to serve a larger population. This is the 2nd exclusive Uro-Nephro hospital in Odisha after AIMS, Bhubaneswar. We remain committed to building a trusted healthcare destination for patients across Eastern India.”

With the launch in Bhubaneswar, AINU extends its presence in Eastern India and its kidney and urology services to patients across Odisha and neighbouring regions.
